body:
Quiet day, one asterisk. The scanner flagged a single cross-platform opportunity today: buying YES on Polymarket's Will Gold hit $4,700 in August (0.073) against NO on Kalshi's Gold above $4,731.99 on Aug 31 (0.920) for a combined cost of $0.993. After fees, the net edge is $0.0018 per contract, with only 60 contracts fillable for a total capturable profit of $0.11 — effectively noise, not a real arbitrage. The two legs aren't actually equivalent bets: Polymarket's contract pays out if gold touches $4,700 at any point during August, while Kalshi's is a settle market checking the spot price only at 5:00 PM ET on August 31, and the strike levels don't even match ($4,700 vs $4,731.99). That mismatch, plus Kalshi's wide bid-ask spread on that strike (0.08/0.09), easily explains the sliver of edge without implying any free money.

Price levels across both venues are internally consistent with where gold actually is. Kalshi's Aug-31 ladder shows yes-bids near 0.98 for above $3,931.99 and roughly a coin-flip around the $4,300–4,400 strikes, which lines up with gold trading in the low-$4,400s in mid-August 2026 after a summer rally driven by soft jobs data and Fed rate-cut expectations: gold prices opened at their highest level since early June following a disappointing employment report that prompted many analysts to pare back expectations of a rate increase. Futures also touched $4,509 overnight this week before pulling back (Gold Hits $4,509 Overnight Then Pulls Back!, Barchart).

Beyond that one flagged pair, order books on both platforms look orderly — no stale quotes, no zero-volume strikes driving false signals, and no other cross-platform mismatches large enough to clear fees. A genuinely quiet day for arbitrage.
headline: One flagged Gold arbitrage is noise, not a real opportunity

sources.title: Gold Hits $4,509 Overnight Then Pulls Back!
